chunks: Truly Safa and Marwa are the symbols of God. Whoever goes on pilgrimage to the House (of God), or on a holy visit, is not guilty of wrong if he walk around them; and he who does good of his own accord will find appreciation with God who knows everything.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk
key_terms.تَطَوَّعَ: Did voluntarily / offered a voluntary deed
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةَ: And Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'i ritual

ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of walking between Safa and Marwa during Hajj?
ai.summary: This verse, known as the Verse of Sa'i, validates the pre-Islamic ritual of circling Safa and Marwa by integrating it into Islamic worship, thereby purifying it from idolatrous connotations. Shia scholars emphasize that its inclusion in Surah Al-Baqarah highlights the continuity of Abrahamic traditions, while the phrase 'man tatawwa'a khayran' underscores the merit of voluntary acts beyond the obligatory rites during Hajj and Umrah.
